A1.g: A. Work that isn't utility work
A1.t: Permits: move agency permits off the contractor
cur: s.7: "Contractor shall obtain and pay for all permits, approvals, clearances and licenses required to perform the Work."

C-1 Note 11: "THE CONTRACTOR SHALL, AT ITS OWN EXPENSE, OBTAIN ALL NECESSARY PERMITS AND LICENSES TO COMPLETE THE PROJECT. OBTAINING PERMITS, OR DELAYS, IS NOT CAUSE FOR DELAY OF THE CONTRACT OR SCHEDULE."
new: s.7: "Contractor shall obtain and pay for the Village of Pleasant Prairie right-of-way / excavation permit(s), any permits required by Contractor's means and methods, and all Diggers Hotline notifications. Owner, through its Engineer, will obtain the WDNR water main extension approval, WPDES construction site stormwater coverage (NOI), the Village erosion control permit, and the WisDOT permit if one is required. Contractor shall comply with the conditions of all permits."
C-1 Note 11: same split, in the sheet's wording. Note 9: change "ALL APPLICABLE PERMITS HAVE BEEN OBTAINED" to "ALL CONTRACTOR PERMITS HAVE BEEN OBTAINED".
A1.why: A utility contractor prices unknown agency approvals and schedule risk he can't control. Pinnacle is already filing the DNR extension.
A1.deliver: Claude drafts the revised manual text (redline) for Pinnacle to drop in; Claude marks up the sheet (clouded PDF) for Pinnacle to revise in CAD

A2.g: A. Work that isn't utility work
A2.t: SWPPP inspections: Pinnacle prices it once, everyone carries the same number
where: Sheet C-6, SWPPP s.5.0 Inspection; General Information
A2.who: Pinnacle (proposal + plan sheet C-6); Owner (bid form)
cur: "INSPECTIONS SHALL BE UNDERTAKEN BY QUALIFIED PERSONNEL PROVIDED BY THE CONTRACTOR ... A STORMWATER POLLUTION PREVENTION PLAN INSPECTION REPORT SHALL BE COMPLETED AND ADDED TO THE SWPPP. RAINFALL SHALL BE RECORDED ON THE SWPPP RAINFALL LOG."
"KEEPING PLANS CURRENT: THE CONTRACTOR SHALL AMEND THE PLAN WHENEVER THERE IS A CHANGE ..."
"CONTRACTOR SHALL SUBMIT A COMPLETED NOTICE OF TERMINATION TO OWNER FOR EXECUTION PRIOR TO THEIR FINAL PAY APPLICATION REQUEST."
new: Pinnacle gives a fixed-fee proposal for SWPPP inspections (every 7 days and within 24 hours of a 1/2" rain), inspection reports, rainfall log, SWPPP amendments, and the Notice of Termination.

Recommended: Zilber contracts Pinnacle directly (add it to Pinnacle's CM estimate under condition 6d). Bid form note: "SWPPP INSPECTION AND REPORTING BY OWNER'S ENGINEER UNDER SEPARATE CONTRACT. CONTRACTOR SHALL MAINTAIN AND REPAIR ALL EROSION CONTROL MEASURES WITHIN 24 HOURS OF NOTICE."

Alternative: carry it in the bid as a fixed allowance line, e.g. "SWPPP inspections by Pinnacle Engineering per proposal dated __/__/__: $______ (all bidders carry this amount)". Contractor pays Pinnacle.
Sheet C-6 s.5.0: "INSPECTIONS SHALL BE UNDERTAKEN BY QUALIFIED PERSONNEL PROVIDED BY THE OWNER'S ENGINEER." Amend-the-plan and Notice of Termination move to the Engineer.
A2.why: Pinnacle gets the work and every bidder carries the same SWPPP cost. Contracting Pinnacle directly avoids a contractor markup on it and keeps the inspector working for you, not the contractor. Either way the Village counts it: condition 7 sizes the security on public improvements plus inspections and construction services.
A2.deliver: Claude drafts the request to Andy for the SWPPP proposal, the bid form note, and the C-6 markup

B1.g: B. Terms that make bidders add money
B1.t: Late-finish exposure: consequential damages + LDs + fees
where: Standard Terms s.5 and s.5a, PDF p.5
cur: "Contractor shall be responsible to Owner for any and all direct or indirect damages (including, but not limited to, consequential damages) incurred as the result of Contractor's failure to complete the Work within the Contract Time. All costs, including attorney's fees, incurred by Owner in enforcing the Agreement ... shall be borne solely by Contractor."
new: Delete both sentences. Keep s.5a liquidated damages ($500/day) as the sole remedy for delay. Art. IV already gives the prevailing party its fees.

B2.g: B. Terms that make bidders add money
cur: "The Owner may, upon written notice, terminate the Agreement, with or without cause, if the Owner determines (in its sole discretion) that the Contractor has not performed ... the Contractor shall not be entitled to receive further payment until the Work is finished."
new: For cause: written notice and 7 days to cure, then Owner may terminate and complete at Contractor's cost. For convenience: Owner pays for work performed and demobilization.
B2.why: "Sole discretion, no pay until finished" reads as risk of not getting paid.
B2.deliver: Claude drafts the revised manual text (redline) for Pinnacle to drop in

B3.g: B. Terms that make bidders add money
cur: "Partial payments ... will be made by the Owner every sixty (60) days ..."

B4.g: B. Terms that make bidders add money
cur: "(iv) Umbrella/excess liability: (a) Each Occurrence in the amount of Five Million Dollars ($5,000,000); and (b) Aggregate ... Five Million Dollars ($5,000,000)."
new: Decision for you. Lisa's only sample is Zilber's certificate for Riley (GC on the Janesville shell building). It is higher than Pinnacle's form on every line: general aggregate $2M (manual $1M), products-completed operations $2M ($1M), auto $2M ($1M), umbrella $10M ($5M), plus employers' liability $1M. Matching it would raise the limits, not lower them.
Options: (a) keep the manual's limits, umbrella $5M; (b) match Zilber's sample; (c) ask Lisa whether a lower standard exists for site work.

Whichever you pick, fix the wording. The manual names the Owner and the Village as additional insured under (i), (ii) and (iii), but (i) is workers' compensation. The sample puts additional insured on general liability only (endorsements CG 2038 and CG 2037) and waives subrogation on general liability and workers' comp. Keep the Village, which the sample does not name. The manual asks for 30 days' written notice of cancellation; the sample only says notice per policy provisions.
B4.why: You asked to see Zilber's insurance first (11/4). Lisa's sample is a Riley certificate, not a utility-contractor standard, and she did not say it applies to site work. The Village as additional insured stays either way (DA approval letter, condition 6c).
B4.deliver: Claude drafts the revised s.9 text (redline) for Pinnacle once you pick a, b or c

B5.why: "All liability" reads as covering the engineer's own design errors.
